cards.explanation: The answer is His name and His Father's name. John says the 144,000 are people “…who had His name and His Father’s name written on their foreheads.” I know a little about having a name put on you, friends. Mine got carved into my handle by the Millers, the family who took me home, and I've been proud of it ever since.

The answer is a new song. John says they “…sang a new song before the throne…” and the sound he hears is like many waters, thunder and harpists strumming their harps. No one could learn the song except the 144,000 who had been redeemed from the earth. I'd pay good money for a front row seat, bakers.
The answer is True. John says, “…no one could learn the song except the 144,000 who had been redeemed from the earth.” Nobody else could pick it up, friends. Not even if they practiced in the shower.

The answer is that they follow the Lamb wherever He goes. John says of the 144,000, “They follow the Lamb wherever He goes.” Wherever He goes is the verse's own wording. No side trips, no shortcuts in that line, bakers. Just following the Lamb (Revelation 14:4).
The answer is False. John says, “And no lie was found in their mouths; they are blameless.” So not one lie was found, friends. My mustache and I are both a little jealous.

The answer is that the hour of His judgment has come. The angel says to fear God and give Him glory, “…because the hour of His judgment has come.” He doesn't whisper it either, bakers. John says he calls it out in a loud voice.
The answer is True. The flying angel says, “Worship the One who made the heavens and the earth and the sea and the springs of waters.” He's pointing everyone to the Maker of all of it, friends.
The answer is that Babylon has fallen. The second angel says, “Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great…” He says the word fallen twice, bakers.

The answer is anger. The third angel warns that anyone who worships the beast and its image and receives its mark on his forehead or on his hand “…will drink the wine of God’s anger…” This is a heavy warning, friends, so let's take it seriously and move on carefully.

The answer is False. The third angel says, “Day and night there is no rest for those who worship the beast and its image…” So no rest, day or night, bakers. It's a heavy line, so I'll just leave it there.

The answer is their perseverance. John writes, “Here is a call for the perseverance of the saints…” These are the saints who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus. Perseverance means sticking with it, friends, like keeping an eye on the oven even when you want to sit down.

The answer is “Blessed are the dead…” who die in the Lord. The voice from heaven tells John to write those words, and it means those who die in the Lord from this moment on. It's a comfort after those heavy warnings, bakers.
The answer is rest. The Spirit says, “they will rest from their labors, for their deeds will follow them.” After a long day of batches, I know how good that word sounds, friends.

The answer is a sharp sickle. John sees One like the Son of Man on the cloud, “…with a golden crown on His head and a sharp sickle in His hand.” Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10). A crown on His head and a sickle in His hand, bakers, and John notes both.
The answer is that the crop of the earth is ripe. The angel cries out, “…the time has come to harvest, for the crop of the earth is ripe.” Ripe is the reason he gives, friends.

The answer is True. The text says, “…the One seated on the cloud swung His sickle over the earth, and the earth was harvested.” The angel's call and the swing go together, bakers. Verse 16 says it plainly.

The answer is clusters of grapes from the vine. The angel from the altar says to “…gather the clusters of grapes from the vine of the earth, because its grapes are ripe.” Grapes, not wheat, friends. This angel is the one with authority over the fire.

The answer is into the great winepress of God's wrath. John says the angel “…gathered the grapes of the earth, and he threw them into the great winepress of God’s wrath.” It's a heavy picture, bakers, so I'll let the verse speak for itself.
The answer is False. John writes, “And the winepress was trodden outside the city…” So it's outside, not inside, friends. It's a heavy part of the passage, and I'll just leave the verse as it is.
